selectionRule: Admitting an evaluated design to the archive does not mean it is the best design. Read the design account, inspect its resources, and compare the final archived selection.

archive.account: The harness this run started from

This agent adds a final-answer normalization middleware plus extractive-QA prompting. The middleware strips markdown, parentheticals, leading "answer:" labels, surrounding quotes and trailing punctuation, legal/university suffixes, and accents before the final answer is recorded; for sentence-like answers it then asks a side LLM to re-read the supplied context and return only the short answer. The system prompt and skill now instruct the model to answer directly from context, prefer the shortest exact span (including "CLUE | ANSWER" lines), return the requested category rather than a more specific entity, give only the requested place, drop trailing common-noun descriptors after names, and keep full creative-work titles while dropping years/subtitles. I expect higher exact-match accuracy because many baseline errors were correct entities wrapped in extra qualifiers, years, descriptors, or full sentences.

archive.account:
This agent replaces surface-only final-answer normalization with a context-grounded answer resolver that runs as a final-answer middleware. It separates the actual question from the supplied context so the question is never treated as evidence, then deterministically recovers Q&A cells from `[PAR]` snippets. The parser ignores `[TLE]` title pipes, joins line-wrapped snippet text, takes the answer cell after the last vertical bar, and strips Jeopardy `right:/wrong:/Value:` trailers, ellipsis-truncated cells, URLs, captions, and dictionary-style metadata. If the question closely matches a clue, it returns that clue's exact answer cell, which fixes partial model answers such as `Bob` → `Bob Mackie` and `Welcome Back` → `Welcome Back, Kotter`.

All candidates are scored by exact token-span context support, answer-line support, and consensus, using grader-aligned normalization that deletes punctuation/removes articles without dropping parenthesized answer content. Side-LLM calls are used only when the current best answer is not already a clean, context-supported short span: two independent side candidates are requested (exact-span extraction and plain short answer), with a third verifier only if they disagree. The final answer is the strongest candidate.

I expect a higher exact-match score because it recovers exact answer cells the main model ignores or truncates, replaces unsupported short paraphrases with context-grounded spans, and avoids second-guessing answers that are already exact, supported short answers.
revisions: This agent replaces the surface-only final-answer normalizer with a context-grounded answer resolver. Before recording a final answer it parses every "CLUE | ANSWER" line from the supplied context, scores candidates by exact/partial context support and exact answer-cell support, and deterministically returns the right-hand-side cell when the question clue or the model's answer matches one. When no deterministic match is confident and the model's answer is not already a supported short span, it asks a side LLM for two independent candidates (exact-span extraction and plain short answer) and, if they disagree, a third verifier call; the final answer is the candidate with strongest context support and consensus. I expect higher exact-match accuracy because it fixes ignored exact answer cells and short-but-unsupported paraphrases while avoiding second-guessing answers that are already exact context spans.

archive.account: This agent adds a precision exact-match layer around the existing normalizer rather than a broad side-LLM ensemble. On the first turn it injects a short evidence brief containing only high-confidence `CLUE | ANSWER` cells, the most relevant context snippets, and a category hint. Its final-answer middleware performs grader-aligned surface cleanup (markdown, quotes, answer labels, trailing punctuation, ASCII folding, and legal/university suffix stripping), exact `CLUE | ANSWER` cell recovery when clue and question strongly match and the model answer is a prefix/subset of the cell, and a small set of general pattern repairs: context-gated singular/plural agreement, `Mount` vs `Mt.` when the context prefers the abbreviation, `Department of the X` vs `the X Department`, and trailing year-parenthetical removal. For bare-title Jeopardy clues it deterministically extracts the implied broad category (state park → state, nationality-based company → country, `Mount X in Y` → country, `Home to ...` → place). Side-LLM re-extraction is used only for long/sentence-like or parenthesized answers that are not already a contiguous context span, with instructions to return the exact context span. I expect this to score higher because it directly repairs the main exact-match failures—missed exact context cells, wrong answer type for title clues, trailing descriptors, and short unsupported paraphrases—without second-guessing short answers that are already context-supported.

On the first turn it injects a short evidence brief containing the best `CLUE | ANSWER` cells, the most relevant context snippets, and a category hint. Its final-answer middleware then applies grader-aligned comparison and a set of high-precision repairs: it removes descriptive words already present in the clue (`Ice hockey` → `hockey`, `Doppler radar` → `Doppler`, `high-speed trains` → `trains`, `multilingual` → `lingual`), fixes singular/plural and possessive forms, recovers the exact context form for `Department of the X` → `the X Department`, and restores parenthesized context answers such as `absorb (the heat)`. For bare-title Jeopardy clues it deterministically extracts the broad category the clue implies (state park → state, nationality-based company → country, `Mount X in Y` → country, `Home to ...` → place), while side-LLM re-extraction is used only for long/sentence-like answers that are not already a contiguous context span. I expect this to score higher because it fixes the main remaining exact-match failures—extra descriptors, wrong answer type, and missed exact context cells—without second-guessing answers that are already short and context-supported.

archive.account: This agent adds a precision final-answer resolver around a direct extractive QA loop. On the first turn, middleware parses the supplied [DOC]/[TLE]/[PAR] context and extracts CLUE | ANSWER cells line-by-line; the strongest matching cells are shown to the model as a numbered menu, so the model replies with just an option number and the final-answer middleware maps that number back to the exact cell text instead of allowing paraphrase drift. The resolver then applies deterministic answer-type reduction (city vs containing state/country, country/state/language/sport/year), a conservative unsupported-answer override from the strongest Q&A cell, and token-aligned exact-span restoration that recovers the original punctuation/case of the matching context span. Side-LLM extraction remains only for long or sentence-like unsupported answers. I expect a higher score because this removes the two most common exact-match failure modes: paraphrase drift and missing/internal punctuation or case mismatches, while the line-by-line Q&A parser prevents multi-cell [PAR] blocks from contaminating the candidate menu.
revisions: This agent adds an exact-answer candidate menu. On the first turn, the middleware extracts the top CLUE | ANSWER cells from the supplied context and presents them as numbered options; the model is prompted to reply with just the option number when one matches. The final-answer middleware maps that number back to the exact answer cell, so the model never has to re-type or paraphrase the winning span. The resolver then performs answer-type reduction (city vs containing state/country, country/state/language/sport/year), a conservative unsupported-answer override from the strongest Q&A cell, and token-aligned exact-span restoration that returns the context's original punctuation/case for otherwise matching answers. Side-LLM extraction remains only for long unsupported answers. I expect a higher score because many remaining exact-match errors are either paraphrase drift or missing punctuation/case; this design removes both by forcing selection from exact context cells and restoring the exact source span.

archive.account: This agent adds a context-constrained span tagger as its final-answer resolver. Instead of asking a side LLM for a free-text short answer, the middleware asks it to return the exact answer substring copied from the supplied context inside <answer> tags; that string is accepted only when it really is a contiguous substring of the context, and is then surface-normalized. A deterministic span index restores the context's original punctuation/case (Mt./Mount, St./Saint), and a capital-gated, local-text prefix detector flags short supported prefixes like "Bob" before "Bob Mackie" or "Welcome Back" before "Welcome Back, Kotter" without re-tagging clean answers like "Shakespeare" before a lowercase verb. The context Q&A parser is line-by-line so multi-cell [PAR] blocks no longer contaminate candidate cells, and tasks with no supplied context are left untouched. It should fix exact-match failures from paraphrasing, partial names, and punctuation drift without second-guessing already-exact short answers.

archive.account: This agent adds a deterministic `context_lookup` tool that, whenever the model is unsure about exact wording, capitalization, punctuation, or the broad category, retrieves verbatim answer spans from the supplied context, preferring `CLUE | ANSWER` cells. The final-answer middleware normalizes wrappers iteratively, then applies exact-match repairs in order: strongest-matching Q&A cell recovery when the model answer is a subset of the cell, exact raw-span copying when tokens match but casing/punctuation differ, and deterministic short-answer repair via the best Q&A cell or nearest exact context span before any side-LLM fallback. Common-noun descriptors such as "University"/"Corporation" are removed only when the bare head is the supported context span and the fuller form is not, so supported exact phrases are preserved. I expect a higher exact-match score because verbatim-span recovery happens earlier and deterministically, reducing paraphrase drift and punctuation/case mismatches without an extra model call, while the context-aware descriptor handling avoids both over-stripping and under-stripping exact context answers.
revisions: This agent adds an on-demand `context_lookup` tool that deterministically retrieves exact answer strings from the supplied context before the final answer is written. The main model is instructed to call it whenever it is unsure of exact wording, capitalization, punctuation, or the expected broad category, and the tool returns only verbatim context spans (preferring line-by-line `CLUE | ANSWER` cells). The final-answer middleware now parses Q&A cells line-by-line with a wrapped-clue buffer, and for short answers that are not already grounded in the context it deterministically repairs them first from the strongest matching Q&A cell and then by copying the closest exact context span with its original punctuation/case, before any side-LLM fallback. I expect a higher exact-match score because this moves exact-span recovery earlier into the agent loop (verbatim copying instead of paraphrase drift) and repairs short unsupported paraphrases and punctuation/case mismatches without asking a side model.

archive.account: This agent replaces the old whole-[PAR] Q&A parser with a line-by-line parser plus BM25/IDF ranking over `CLUE | ANSWER` cells, so every cell in a multi-cell snippet becomes a candidate and the cell whose clue best matches the question is ranked first. Its final-answer middleware restores the exact context punctuation/case of supported spans while preserving leading articles (e.g. The Hague) and preferring [PAR]/answer-cell occurrences over [TLE] title abbreviations, applies context-gated descriptor stripping, and deterministically repairs explicit country/state/year questions using correct multi-word names (United States, South Africa, New York, North Carolina, etc.). When the model's answer is still not a contiguous context span, it asks a side LLM a grounded multiple-choice question over the top parsed cells and maps the returned option number back to the exact cell text, instead of using free-text side extraction; only as a last resort does it allow tagged extraction that must be a contiguous context substring. The same final-answer middleware now also runs on forced answers after the turn budget, so those answers get exact-span recovery and repairs too. I expect a higher exact-match score because it recovers far more exact answer cells, removes paraphrase drift from the side model, preserves abbreviation punctuation, and only second-guesses supported short answers when a near-identical clue cell proves them wrong.

archive.account: This agent keeps the previous deterministic final-answer repairs but changes the repair path in three ways. (1) Its context Q&A parser works line-by-line and keeps the enclosing [TLE] title, so every CLUE | ANSWER cell in a multi-cell [PAR] block becomes a candidate; it only parses snippets whose [TLE] or text actually looks like a Jeopardy/Q&A transcript (title hints such as "jeopardy"/"J! Archive", or explicit right:/wrong:/value: markers), so ordinary pipe-separated dictionary/shopping text is not mistaken for a clue-answer cell. It also joins a short answer cell that is wrapped across a newline only when the continuation is lowercase and ends at an explicit `....` or `|` boundary, so wrapped cells such as `a timing gun` are recovered without merging the next clue. Title-implicit clues ("This food ..." under [TLE] "Pizza") are scored against title+clue. (2) When the repaired answer is not a clean, context-supported span, the middleware does not immediately call the side model; it returns a continue action asking the main model (which still has the full context) to re-answer, optionally by selecting a letter from a small menu of exact context candidates. The selected letter maps back to the exact context string. Only if that revision still leaves an unsupported answer does the side-model fallback run. (3) Deterministic repairs restore the original punctuation/case of supported token spans, lower the Q&A-cell recovery threshold for prefix/subset answers ("Bob" -> "Bob Mackie"), and tasks with no supplied context receive only surface cleanup rather than being treated as self-evidence. I expect a higher exact-match score because it recovers more exact cells (including wrapped and non-final cells) while avoiding fake Q&A cells from non-Jeopardy text, uses the stronger main model for the first repair attempt, avoids second-guessing clean supported short answers, and preserves exact context casing/punctuation.

This agent replaces the empty SearchQA skill with a structured evidence-grounding protocol: it identifies the expected answer type and exact answer slot, filters noisy snippets for direct relevance (treating Jeopardy/QA archive lines as strong evidence), scores candidates by directness/specificity/agreement, verifies the chosen answer by substituting it back into the question, and outputs only the shortest well-formed answer with exact evidence wording, date granularity matched to the question, plain ASCII, and no markdown or explanatory glosses. It also matches person-name form to the strongest evidence rather than always expanding surnames to full names. I expect it to score higher because it suppresses distractors, over-answers, and format errors while preserving the exact reference forms that exact-match grading rewards.

archive.account: This agent replaces simple relevance scoring with constraint-resolution: it parses each clue into independent factual constraints, scores every snippet by which constraints it supports or contradicts, joins anchor and partial snippets to form candidates, and ranks by constraint coverage rather than mention frequency. It only falls back to parametric knowledge when snippets fail to name an answer and the model has a crisp, snippet-consistent entity. I expect it to score higher because many SearchQA errors come from picking a frequently mentioned but only partial candidate; requiring whole-clue satisfaction suppresses those distractors and improves multi-hop clues.

archive.account: This agent keeps the evidence-grounding strengths of the current leader and replaces single-pass candidate scoring with a three-channel ensemble plus verification. It independently generates candidates from (A) literal clue-answer archive lines, (B) evidence synthesis over directly relevant snippets, and (C) a gated independent memory probe. Each candidate is verified against the question's own facts; snippet disagreement alone does not discard a correct candidate. Reconciliation is a confidence-gated vote: exact archive answer first, then two-channel agreement, then synthesis, then memory, then the best snippet-supported candidate. This preserves exact reference wording for exact-match grading while reducing wrong distractor picks and avoidable "unknown" outputs when evidence is weak.

Everest, Of Mice and Men) while still rejecting multi-sentence prose. The skill is rewritten as a slot-first, clue-shape router: it identifies the exact grammatical slot (number, possessives, function words), subtracts descriptors already stated in the question, and routes bare-title, quote, year-event, and translation clues differently instead of treating every clue as the same entity lookup. It then verifies candidates under grader-aligned normalization (lowercase, ASCII, no punctuation, no a/an/the), preserving token order, abbreviations like Mt./Mount, and evidence name forms. I expect a higher exact-match score because the pre-parser improves evidence retrieval while the slot router fixes the most common remaining error class: semantically right answers with extra descriptor words or the wrong surface form.

archive.account: This agent keeps evidence grounding and deterministic pre-extraction, and adds a slot-contract compiler to the UserPromptSubmit hook. For every question it classifies the answer slot as ENTITY, TYPE_OF, COMPLETION, or BARE_CLUE and injects that contract before the model reads the snippets. COMPLETION is gated on an explicit blank, a leading-ellipsis fragment, or an explicit completion cue, so quoted title/quote clues are not misread as fill-in-the-blank. It also cleans and slot-normalizes extracted CLUE|ANSWER cells: truncating appended titles, deterministically stripping only the clearly removable category suffixes (gland, missile), leaving legal/company suffixes to be judged against the evidence rather than blindly deleted, accepting short direct clues like "this gland", and tagging one-token person answers as EXACT-PARTIAL. The skill treats EXACT cells as decisive and obeys the slot contract, so the model emits the required surface form—the named entity without a repeated category noun, only the missing completion text, or the full subtype phrase when the evidence/idiom requires it—instead of over-answering with descriptors or blindly copying an archive cell with a category suffix. I expect it to score higher because the remaining errors at 0.815 are mostly surface-form and slot-boundary mistakes, and this design moves that calibration into deterministic preprocessing while preserving exact reference wording and avoiding blind suffix deletion for names like East River or First Amendment.

archive.account: This agent keeps the slot contract and exact pre-extracted clue=>answer lines, and adds a conservative deterministic candidate-consensus block computed by the UserPromptSubmit hook. The hook clusters every extracted QA cell by grader-normalized answer, merges surname-only person aliases into fuller name forms only when the surname is an unambiguous suffix (for this-person and pronoun/"who" person slots), counts exact clue matches, independent snippet support, and cell support, then emits a short ranked vote. It deliberately omits singleton close-only cells from the vote—those stay as pre-extracted evidence lines—so one noisy flashcard/prose split cannot become a false consensus. Person clusters whose exact cell is a one-token name are tagged EXACT-PARTIAL in the consensus as well. The skill reads the block as evidence rather than a command: a clear rank-1 lead is decisive, close ranks force whole-clue re-solving. I expect higher accuracy because the model no longer has to mentally aggregate scattered paraphrase cells; it sees majority support explicitly, which suppresses frequently mentioned partial distractors and fixes person-name surface-form errors without abandoning exact evidence wording.

archive.account: This agent keeps the leader's slot contract and exact pre-extracted CLUE|ANSWER cells, and adds a deterministic token-aligned prose layer to the UserPromptSubmit hook. For each ordinary snippet sentence it computes the longest common subsequence between the clue's content tokens and the sentence tokens using the same punctuation-split tokenization, then re-emits the top clue-covering sentences with already-stated clue words double-bracketed so the missing answer is visually adjacent.
